t: HALO: Loop-aware Bootstrapping Management for Fully Homomorphic Encryption
pb: FHE programs using repeated multiplications deplete the ciphertext noise budget (level), requiring bootstrapping to reset it; existing compiler-based bootstrapping placement tools cannot handle loops, severely limiting automated support for practical FHE programs that use iterative constructs.
me: HALO is a compiler that extends automatic bootstrapping placement to programs containing loops. It performs loop-aware level analysis to track ciphertext noise levels across loop iterations, determines the minimum set of bootstrapping operations required to prevent level underflow throughout the loop body and across all iterations, and inserts them automatically. The compiler reasons about loop-carried level dependencies to place bootstrapping at loop boundaries or within the loop body only where necessary.
nv: First compiler to support automatic bootstrapping placement inside loops for FHE programs, enabling safe and efficient execution of iterative encrypted computations without programmer intervention.

mx.other: Specific performance numbers not stated in abstract; reduction in programming burden is the primary claim

th: Loop-aware automatic bootstrapping placement for FHE programs

t: Treelet Accelerated Ray Tracing on GPUs
pb: GPU ray tracing suffers from poor memory access locality because rays traverse a BVH tree in divergent order, causing excessive DRAM traffic; while treelet-based traversal (grouping BVH subtrees and batching rays per treelet) reduces memory traffic on specialized accelerators, applying it to GPUs is non-trivial and naive implementations are ineffective.
me: The paper proposes Virtualized Treelet Queues with two main components. First, ray virtualization terminates raygen shaders after issuing their trace-ray instruction to free CUDA cores, increasing the number of rays concurrently in flight and enabling more cache reuse within treelets. Second, a dynamic treelet queue architecture switches between traversal modes (intra-treelet vs. inter-treelet) at runtime to maximize efficiency. Additionally, warp repacking is applied to the RT unit to improve SIMT efficiency during treelet traversal.
nv: Ray virtualization that reclaims CUDA cores from waiting raygen shaders to multiply in-flight rays, paired with a dynamic treelet queue to exploit the resulting cache reuse—achieving 95% average speedup on a baseline GPU with hardware RT acceleration.

mx.speedup: 95% average speedup vs. baseline GPU with RT acceleration (LumiBench, path tracing, 1 spp, 3 bounces)

th: Treelet-based BVH traversal with ray virtualization for GPU ray tracing

t: Cinnamon: A Framework for Scale-Out Encrypted AI
pb: Fully homomorphic encryption (FHE) imposes orders-of-magnitude performance overhead for ML inference, and prior FHE accelerators use massive monolithic chip designs that do not scale to large models like BERT and provide poor performance-per-dollar.
me: Cinnamon is a scale-out FHE acceleration framework that exploits parallelism at all program levels using novel algorithms, a compiler, and a chiplet-based hardware design. The compiler identifies and schedules FHE operation parallelism (polynomial NTT, RNS decomposition, key-switching) across multiple chips, while architectural extensions reduce per-chip resource requirements to enable economical scaling. Novel algorithms reduce communication volume between chiplets, enabling a distributed multi-chip FHE accelerator rather than a single monolithic die.
nv: Scale-out chiplet architecture for FHE acceleration with a co-designed compiler and algorithms that distribute FHE polynomial arithmetic across multiple chips, enabling the first feasible FHE inference for large LLMs like BERT.

mx.speedup: 36,600x over CPU; 2.3x over prior state-of-the-art FHE accelerator
mx.ppa: 5x perf/$ vs monolithic; 2.68x perf/$ vs chiplet SotA
mx.other: BERT FHE inference: 17 hours (CPU) -> 1.67 seconds

th: scale-out FHE acceleration for encrypted AI inference

t: Accelerating Number Theoretic Transform with Multi-GPU Systems for Efficient Zero Knowledge Proof
pb: Number Theoretic Transform (NTT), a key bottleneck in zero-knowledge proof generation, has not been efficiently parallelized across multiple GPUs because its butterfly permutation access pattern generates high inter-GPU communication overhead that offsets the compute gains from additional GPUs.
me: The paper redesigns the NTT algorithm for multi-GPU execution by restructuring the butterfly computation stages to localize data access within GPU memory and minimize the frequency and volume of inter-GPU data transfers. The approach introduces a GPU-topology-aware permutation schedule that maps NTT stages to GPU assignments so that communication-intensive permutation steps are batched and overlap-optimized with computation. NVLink or PCIe interconnect topology is leveraged to select inter-GPU transfer paths that maximize aggregate bandwidth.
nv: GPU-topology-aware NTT stage mapping that restructures butterfly permutations to minimize inter-GPU communication overhead and enable scalable multi-GPU NTT for ZK proof generation.

mx.other: Multi-GPU NTT speedup over single-GPU baseline (details in full paper)

th: multi-GPU NTT acceleration for zero-knowledge proofs

t: BQSim: GPU-accelerated Batch Quantum Circuit Simulation using Decision Diagram
pb: Existing quantum circuit simulators process one input state at a time, but applications such as quantum testing and verification require simulating a circuit under multiple input states (batch simulation). No GPU-accelerated batch quantum circuit simulator exists that exploits shared structure across inputs.
me: BQSim uses decision diagrams (DDs) to compactly represent quantum gate matrices and identify shared structure across batch inputs, then converts the DD representation into a GPU-efficient data structure for parallel evaluation. A task-graph-based execution engine minimizes repetitive GPU kernel launch overhead by grouping related computations into batched kernel calls and overlapping kernel execution with data movement between host and device. The DD optimization step reduces the total computation needed for batch simulation by collapsing redundant operations shared across inputs.
nv: Combining decision-diagram-based circuit optimization for shared-structure exploitation with a GPU-efficient data structure and task-graph execution engine to achieve the first GPU-accelerated batch quantum circuit simulator.

mx.speedup: 3.25x over cuQuantum; 159.06x over Qiskit Aer; 311.42x over FlatDD (average)

th: GPU-accelerated batch quantum circuit simulation via decision diagrams

t: CIPHERMATCH: Accelerating Homomorphic Encryption-Based String Matching via Memory-Efficient Data Packing and In-Flash Processing
pb: Homomorphic encryption (HE)-based exact string matching incurs prohibitive computational latency due to expensive HE operations (multiplication, rotation) and severe data movement overhead from the large ciphertext memory footprint. Prior HE string matching algorithms cannot efficiently handle these combined bottlenecks.
me: CIPHERMATCH is an algorithm-hardware co-design that (1) applies an optimized software-based data packing scheme to reduce ciphertext memory footprint, (2) reformulates the string matching algorithm to eliminate costly HE multiplications and rotations, replacing them with cheaper addition-only operations, and (3) introduces a new in-flash processing (IFP) architecture that performs computation near the flash storage to minimize data movement between memory and processor.
nv: Combining HE-algorithm redesign to remove multiplicative operations with a purpose-built in-flash processing architecture that eliminates DRAM-level data movement for encrypted string matching.

mx.other: not stated in abstract; paper claims latency and data movement reduction vs prior HE string matching

th: near-storage HE acceleration for encrypted string matching

t: Harmonia: A Unified Framework for Heterogeneous FPGA Acceleration in the Cloud
pb: The shell-role FPGA architecture adopted by cloud providers works well for homogeneous FPGA servers but fails to handle heterogeneous FPGA configurations: prior solutions either require laborious shell development for each FPGA variant (provider burden) or ad-hoc software modifications for each application (user burden), with no portable abstraction across diverse cloud FPGA types.
me: Harmonia introduces a unified framework that abstracts cloud FPGA heterogeneity at both the hardware and software levels. On the hardware side, it defines a standardized shell interface specification that decouples platform-specific shell logic from portable role logic, allowing roles (user accelerators) to be written once and ported across heterogeneous FPGAs. On the software side, Harmonia provides a resource management layer and a driver abstraction that hides FPGA-specific differences from user applications, enabling portability without per-FPGA software modifications.
nv: A unified shell interface specification and software abstraction layer that decouples portable accelerator roles from platform-specific shells across heterogeneous cloud FPGA families.

mx.other: not stated in abstract

th: unified shell abstraction for heterogeneous cloud FPGA management

t: ReSBM: Region-based Scale and Minimal-Level Bootstrapping Management for FHE via Min-Cut
pb: In RNS-CKKS fully homomorphic encryption, repeated homomorphic multiplications escalate ciphertext scale and consume multiplicative levels, requiring expensive bootstrapping to restore capacity; existing compile-time approaches do not efficiently minimize the number and placement of bootstrapping operations, leading to excess overhead in encrypted ML inference.
me: ReSBM partitions the FHE computation graph into regions using a min-cut graph algorithm that identifies the minimal set of bootstrapping insertion points needed to prevent ciphertext level overflow. Within each region, scale management is handled to keep multiplicative levels within bounds. The min-cut formulation finds a provably minimal-bootstrapping schedule at compile time, reducing the number of costly bootstrapping operations without sacrificing correctness. This is coupled with region-level scale assignment to prevent capacity overflow throughout encrypted inference.
nv: Framing FHE bootstrapping placement as a min-cut problem on the computation graph to find a provably minimal bootstrapping schedule at compile time.

mx.other: reduced number of bootstrapping operations vs prior approaches (not quantified in abstract)

th: Min-cut-based bootstrapping minimization for FHE encrypted inference

t: BatchZK: A Fully Pipelined GPU-Accelerated System for Batch Generation of Zero-Knowledge Proofs
pb: GPU-accelerated zero-knowledge proof (ZKP) systems optimize for low single-proof latency but do not support high-throughput batch proof generation, creating a bottleneck for applications like blockchain and verifiable ML that require generating many proofs concurrently.
me: BatchZK constructs a fully pipelined GPU execution engine for batch ZKP generation. The pipeline overlaps the multiple stages of proof generation (e.g., polynomial commitment, multi-scalar multiplication, NTT) across multiple concurrent proofs using GPU streams and memory management strategies that keep GPU compute units busy throughout. By co-scheduling proofs at different stages simultaneously on the GPU, BatchZK amortizes memory transfer and kernel launch overhead across the batch, maximizing GPU throughput. The system targets standard ZKP schemes (e.g., Groth16 or PLONK-family) that underpin modern blockchain applications.
nv: Full pipeline parallelism across independent ZKP generation tasks on GPU, turning the sequential single-proof flow into a throughput-optimized batch pipeline for the first time.

mx.other: throughput improvement over single-proof GPU systems (not quantified in abstract)

th: Pipelined GPU batch zero-knowledge proof generation

t: HetEC: Architectures for Heterogeneous Quantum Error Correction Codes
pb: Surface codes for quantum error correction scale quadratically in physical overhead with the number of correctable errors, making them resource-prohibitive at scale. Quantum LDPC (qLDPC) codes offer superior scaling but lack a clear path to universal logical computation on their own; no architecture jointly exploits both code families.
me: HetEC designs quantum computer architectures that combine surface codes and qLDPC codes in a heterogeneous manner. Surface code regions handle operations requiring local topological structure and magic state distillation for universal gate sets, while qLDPC code regions provide superior error-correction scaling. The architecture defines interfaces and protocols for logical qubit transfer and gate teleportation between code boundaries, enabling universal logical computation across the heterogeneous fabric.
nv: A heterogeneous quantum architecture that systematically combines surface codes and qLDPC codes to achieve universal logical computation while accessing the distinct resource trade-offs of each code family.

mx.other: not stated in abstract

th: heterogeneous quantum error correction architectures combining surface codes and qLDPC codes

t: UniZK: Accelerating Zero-Knowledge Proof with Unified Hardware and Flexible Kernel Mapping
pb: Emerging hash-function-based ZKP protocols introduce diverse computation kernels (NTT, hash functions, general polynomial arithmetic) that existing ZKP accelerators cannot efficiently support, since prior designs target only elliptic-curve-based protocols with dedicated per-kernel hardware units that waste area and underutilize resources for multi-kernel workloads.
me: UniZK uses a systolic-array-based hardware architecture enhanced with extra local links and a new vector processing mode that makes the array flexible enough to serve as a unified substrate for diverse ZKP kernels. Novel mapping strategies are developed to map NTT, hash functions, and general polynomial computations onto this unified hardware, ensuring high resource utilization without dedicated per-kernel units. Smart kernel mapping strategies handle the varied data flow and compute patterns of each primitive.
nv: A systolic-array architecture extended with local links and a vector mode that serves as a unified, highly utilized hardware substrate for all ZKP kernels via flexible mapping, eliminating the need for dedicated per-kernel units.

mx.speedup: 97x over CPU, 46x over GPU (same protocols); 840x over prior ZKP ASICs (different protocols)

th: Unified ASIC acceleration for diverse ZKP protocols

t: Micro Blossom: Accelerated Minimum-Weight Perfect Matching Decoding for Quantum Error Correction
pb: Minimum-Weight Perfect Matching (MWPM) decoders for quantum error correction (QEC) on surface codes require sub-microsecond latency to avoid accumulating idle logical errors during fault-tolerant gate feedforward, but all prior exact MWPM implementations on CPUs achieve multi-microsecond latency and the blossom algorithm was believed to be too complex for hardware acceleration. Approximate decoders that achieve low latency sacrifice accuracy, causing 1.7x-13.9x more logical errors at code distance 13.
me: Micro Blossom employs a heterogeneous CPU+FPGA architecture that partitions the blossom algorithm into primal (CPU) and dual (hardware) phases. The FPGA accelerator instantiates one vertex processing unit (vPU) and one edge processing unit (ePU) per node and edge in the decoding graph, achieving O(d^3) parallel PUs. The dual phase—the dominant bottleneck—is fully parallelized: each vPU maintains compact per-vertex state (residue, unique-touch, unique-node, direction) and communicates only with graph neighbors via a broadcast/convergecast network. Isolated conflicts (the common case at low error rates) are detected and resolved entirely in hardware without CPU involvement via parallel ePU logic, reducing average CPU interactions from O(p*|V|+1) to O(p^2*|V|+1). Round-wise fusion processes each measurement round incrementally as it arrives, achieving stream decoding with constant latency independent of the number of rounds. The hardware is generated from a decoding-graph JSON specification via SpinalHDL to synthesizable Verilog.
nv: The first hardware-accelerated exact MWPM decoder: a per-vertex/per-edge parallel processing unit architecture implementing the blossom algorithm's dual phase entirely in programmable logic, combined with hardware-resident isolated-conflict resolution and round-wise fusion for sub-microsecond stream decoding.

mx.speedup: 8x lower average decoding latency than best prior MWPM (Sparse Blossom) at d=13, p=0.1%
mx.area: Xilinx Versal VMK180 FPGA prototype; O(d^3) PUs for surface code distance d
mx.accuracy: Exact MWPM (same logical error rate as software Parity Blossom); 17x total latency reduction vs. Parity Blossom CPU baseline
mx.other: Average decoding latency 0.8 us at d=13, p=0.1% at 62 MHz; worst-case complexity O(d^9) vs. O(d^12) prior

th: hardware-accelerated quantum error correction decoding

t: Fat-Tree QRAM: A High-Bandwidth Shared Quantum Random Access Memory for Parallel Queries
pb: Existing Quantum Random Access Memory (QRAM) architectures, particularly Bucket-Brigade (BB) QRAM, cannot process multiple queries in parallel because the binary tree root node is exclusively occupied for the entire duration of each query, forcing all queries to queue and execute sequentially. In a shared memory system with multiple QPUs, this causes total query latency to scale as O(p*log(N)) for p parallel processes, bottlenecking parallel quantum algorithms.
me: Fat-Tree QRAM replaces each single router node in the BB QRAM binary tree with a Fat-Tree node containing multiple router copies: the router at level i is duplicated (log(N)-i-1) times, so the root contains log(N) router copies and the leaves contain one (matching BB QRAM). This doubling of total router count (from N to 2N-2-log(N)) enables O(log(N)) independent queries to be pipelined simultaneously. Each query is realized via alternating gate steps (CSWAP address loading, 4 circuit layers each) and swap steps (local intra-node SWAP gates, 1 layer each, constant depth because swaps are nearest-neighbor within a node). Two local swap types (SWAP-I and SWAP-II, alternating even/odd router indices) cycle queries through sub-component QRAMs of increasing size without inter-node communication. Hardware is implemented in both modular (superconducting coaxial-cable-linked chips) and on-chip (bi-planar thickness-2 chip with TSVs for inter-plane connections) formats using superconducting cavities with native CSWAP gates. A FIFO scheduling protocol (proven optimal by greedy exchange) maximizes utilization.
nv: The Fat-Tree QRAM architecture that achieves O(log(N)) query-level pipelining in O(log(N)) time using O(N) qubits by replacing binary-tree BB QRAM nodes with multiplexed Fat-Tree nodes, achieving constant QRAM bandwidth independent of memory size N.

mx.speedup: up to 10x circuit depth reduction for parallel quantum algorithms vs. BB and Virtual QRAM at N=2^10
mx.area: 16N qubits (vs. 8N for BB QRAM) — 2x qubit overhead for log(N)-fold parallelism
mx.accuracy: same infidelity scaling as BB QRAM: O(log^2(N)*epsilon) per query
mx.other: constant QRAM bandwidth (independent of N) vs. O(1/log(N)) for BB QRAM; amortized single-query latency 8.25 circuit layers (constant) vs. 8*log(N) for BB

th: high-bandwidth parallel-query quantum random access memory

t: Optimizing Quantum Circuits, Fast and Slow
pb: Quantum circuit optimization requires balancing two complementary approaches: fast rewrite-rule passes (local pattern matching, low quality) and slow unitary synthesis (global search over circuit space, high quality but exponential cost), but these have been treated as disjoint techniques without a unified framework that exploits their synergies. No prior optimizer systematically combines the two in a way that achieves better quality than either alone.
me: The paper presents a unifying framework that models rewriting and resynthesis as abstract circuit transformation operators on subcircuits. The algorithm 'guoq' alternates between fast rewrite-rule passes (which simplify local patterns and create resynthesis opportunities) and targeted unitary synthesis (applied to subcircuits identified as high-gain by the rewriting pass). Resynthesis is applied to subcircuits of bounded size where exhaustive search is tractable, guided by the rewriting pass which determines which regions are best candidates. This fast-slow interleaving lets rewriting decompose the circuit into manageable blocks for synthesis, while synthesis achieves global optima that local rules cannot reach.
nv: A unified abstract circuit transformation framework where fast rewrite rules and slow unitary synthesis are composed as first-class operators, enabling the guoq algorithm to exploit the synergies of both approaches for stronger circuit optimization than either alone.

mx.accuracy: strongly outperforms existing optimizers on wide benchmark range (specific gate-count reductions not in abstract)
mx.other: circuit gate count reduction vs. state-of-the-art optimizers

th: unified fast+slow quantum circuit optimization via rewriting and resynthesis

t: Pirate: No Compromise Low-Bandwidth VR Streaming for Edge Devices
pb: High-quality VR streaming for edge devices requires simultaneously satisfying two competing demands: extremely low bandwidth (the edge uplink is constrained) and real-time rendering at high frame rates (90 FPS), while previous approaches sacrifice one for the other.
me: Pirate exploits stereo similarity—the high structural redundancy between left-eye and right-eye VR video frames—to avoid transmitting both views. Only one eye's view is transmitted at any time, alternating left and right, together with precomputed disparity maps and optical flow information. The target eye view is iteratively synthesized on-device from the single transmitted view using only this lightweight geometric information (no large ML model), at extremely low bitrates down to 0.1 bits per pixel. The alternating transmission schedule further amortizes bandwidth by recycling synthesized frames across time.
nv: Iterative stereo view synthesis using only disparity and optical flow—without large ML models—enabling real-time VR streaming at 90 FPS under bandwidths as low as 0.1 bpp on edge devices.

mx.other: 20%–40% bandwidth reduction vs. prior approaches; similar quality maintained

th: Low-bandwidth real-time VR stereo streaming via stereo similarity exploitation

t: Qubit Movement-Optimized Program Generation on Zoned Neutral Atom Processors
pb: Zoned neutral atom quantum architectures segregate execution spaces for 1- and 2-qubit gates, but naively scheduled programs incur excessive intra-zone atom movement, consuming most execution time in traveling rather than computation.
me: Mantra rewrites quantum programs using three strategies: fountain-shaped controlled-Z (CZ) chains to group gates, ZZ-interaction protocol to eliminate interleaved 1-qubit gates, and preemptive gate scheduling. Jointly optimizes gate ordering and zone assignment to minimize atom movements.
nv: Fountain-shaped CZ chain topology and ZZ-interaction protocol to decouple 1- and 2-qubit gate execution streams, reducing zone transitions.

mx.speedup: 68% movement reduction, 35% gate reduction, 17% fidelity gain

th: quantum circuit optimization for zoned neutral atoms

t: Vectron: A Dynamic Programming Auto-vectorization Framework
pb: Dynamic programming algorithms (especially sequence alignment) are computation bottlenecks in genomics and other fields; hand-vectorization is tedious and error-prone. Auto-vectorization of array-based DP code is needed.
me: Vectron targets Python array-based DP implementations and auto-converts to vectorized C++ equivalents exploiting SIMD (CPU) and GPU parallelism. Processes multiple problem instances in parallel using SIMD/GPU primitives without requiring algorithm modifications.
nv: Automatic vectorization of array-based DP from Python to SIMD/GPU-accelerated code without algorithm changes.
th: auto-vectorization of dynamic programming algorithms

t: Qiwu: Exploiting Ciphertext-Level SIMD Parallelism in Homomorphic Encryption Programs
pb: Fully Homomorphic Encryption (FHE) with CKKS scheme enables secure computation on encrypted data, but reduction operations create large bubbles (gaps) in intermediate ciphertexts that waste computational resources despite plaintext-level SIMD packing.
me: Qiwu performs ciphertext-level vectorization by fusing multiple ciphertexts containing bubbles to eliminate gaps in output ciphertexts. A DSL specifies zero bubbles in inputs and nonzero bubbles in outputs; data-flow analysis tracks bubble patterns and a cost-benefit assessment guides fusion decisions.
nv: Introducing ciphertext-level fusion for bubble elimination in FHE programs, complementing plaintext-level SIMD parallelism.
th: Ciphertext-level fusion for FHE bubble elimination

t: Late Breaking Results: Encoder-Decoder Generative Diffusion Transformer Towards Push-Button Analog IC Sizing
pb: Analog IC sizing relies on time-consuming optimization-based methods that lack scalability and generalization to unseen performance targets.
me: Encoder-decoder diffusion transformer (attention-based generative model) solves inverse analog sizing problem by sampling accurate solutions at push-button speed, trained on performance targets to generalize beyond training set.
nv: Generative diffusion models with encoder-decoder transformer backbone for fast analog IC sizing with superior generalization.

mx.other: push-button speed sampling vs optimization

th: Generative diffusion transformer for automated analog IC sizing

t: EdgeMM: Multi-Core CPU with Heterogeneous AI-Extension and Activation-aware Weight Pruning for Multimodal LLMs at Edge
pb: Multimodal LLMs combine compute-intensive modality encoders with memory-bound LLM decoders, presenting distinct performance bottlenecks that homogeneous CPU designs cannot address efficiently.
me: EdgeMM uses multi-core CPU with heterogeneous AI coprocessors: compute-centric systolic arrays for encoders and memory-centric digital compute-in-memory (CIM) for decoders. Dynamic activation-aware weight pruning and bandwidth management optimize efficiency. Implemented in 22nm commercial technology.
nv: Heterogeneous CPU with dual coprocessor types (systolic + CIM) matched to encoder/decoder workload characteristics.
th: Heterogeneous CPU for multimodal LLM edge inference

t: Fast End-to-End Simulation and Exploration of Many-RISCV-Core Baseband Transceivers for Software-Defined Radio-Access Networks
pb: Designing high-performance many-core SDR processors for baseband processing requires functional validation and end-to-end performance analysis within realistic wireless environments, but RTL simulation is prohibitively slow.
me: Fast simulation framework using static binary translation with approximate timing model of many-core hardware (1024 RISC-V cores), coupled to wireless channel models. Simulates critical physical layer 5G OFDM detection functions. Single-threaded: 9.5s-3min per symbol (3 OOM faster than RTL); parallelizable to 128 threads with 73-121x speedup.
nv: Binary translation-based simulator with fast timing model for rapid end-to-end SDR baseband processor exploration.

mx.speedup: 3 OOM faster than RTL; 73-121x with parallelization

th: Fast simulation of many-core RISC-V SDR baseband processors

t: Enhancing LLM-based Quantum Code Generation with Multi-Agent Optimization and Quantum Error Correction
pb: LLM-based quantum code generation struggles with fault-tolerance and correctness; general-purpose LLM techniques (CoT, RAG) don't translate to quantum domain without domain-specific optimization.
me: Multi-agent framework where each agent targets specific quantum optimizations (error correction, circuit synthesis); semantic analyzer with multi-pass inference; integrates structured Chain-of-Thought and error correction decoder; test suite measuring per-agent contribution.
nv: First multi-agent LLM framework tailored to quantum code generation with integrated error correction and domain-specific optimization.
th: Quantum-specific multi-agent LLM code generation with error correction

t: P-DAC: Power-Efficient Photonic Accelerators for LLM Inference
pb: Optical analog computing accelerators (e.g., LighteningTransformer) require electrical DAC control to modulate optical intensity modulators; DAC power consumption significantly undermines energy efficiency of photonic systems.
me: P-DAC solution reducing DAC power consumption in optical accelerator control loop; optimizes electrical modulation of Mach-Zehnder modulators and DAC efficiency.

t: Configurable DSP-Based CAM Architecture for Data-Intensive Applications on FPGAs
pb: FPGA-based Content-Addressable Memory (CAM) implementations suffer from high LUT/BRAM resource utilization, limited scalability, and suboptimal performance due to inefficient parallel search operations.
me: Novel DSP-block-based CAM architecture leverages digital signal processing blocks' built-in storage and logic capabilities as the core resource. DSP blocks efficiently implement parallel content search and multi-query support. Configuration parameters allow application-specific tuning of CAM width, depth, and search parallelism.
nv: First FPGA CAM architecture using DSP blocks as primary resources, enabling configurable multi-query support with reduced search/update latency and improved scalability.

t: Scalable Community Detection Using Quantum Hamiltonian Descent and QUBO Formulation
pb: Community detection in large-scale graph data is computationally expensive with classical optimization; existing approaches lack scalability for diverse graph sizes and structures.
me: The approach reformulates community detection as a Quadratic Unconstrained Binary Optimization (QUBO) problem and applies Quantum Hamiltonian Descent (QHD) to find optimal community structures. A multi-level algorithm iteratively refines community assignments by alternating between QUBO setup and QHD-based optimization.
nv: First hybrid quantum-inspired algorithm combining QHD with QUBO formulation for scalable community detection in large-scale graphs.
th: Quantum Hamiltonian Descent for scalable community detection

t: EPOC: An Efficient Pulse Generation Framework with Advanced Synthesis for Quantum Circuits
pb: Quantum optimal control has high computational overhead and generates long circuit latencies; gate-based pulse generation requires substantial resource overhead.
me: EPOC combines ZX-Calculus, circuit partitioning, and advanced circuit synthesis for efficient pulse generation. The approach implements finer granularity in pulse generation and explores equivalent circuit representations to increase parallelism. ZX-Calculus enables compact circuit abstraction and optimization, while partitioning allows parallel processing of circuit segments.
nv: First framework combining ZX-Calculus with circuit partitioning and synthesis for low-overhead, high-parallelism quantum pulse generation.

mx.latency: 31.74% reduction vs. prior work; 76.80% vs. gate-based

th: ZX-Calculus-based pulse generation with circuit partitioning

t: ZXNet: ZX Calculus-Driven Graph Neural Network Framework for Quantum Circuit Equivalence Checking
pb: Quantum circuits require transpilation into hardware-compatible instructions, significantly altering designs; existing equivalence checking methods struggle with scalability and computational overhead.
me: ZXNet integrates ZX calculus with graph neural networks for quantum circuit equivalence checking. ZX calculus provides compact graph abstractions of quantum circuits, while GNNs capture complex equivalence patterns by learning both local and global circuit features. The framework leverages ZX-based graph representations to reduce dimensionality and complexity of the equivalence checking problem.
nv: First framework combining ZX calculus-based graph abstractions with GNNs for scalable quantum circuit equivalence verification.
th: ZX calculus-driven GNN for quantum circuit verification

t: ArbiterQ: Improving QNN Convergency and Accuracy by Applying Personalized Model on Heterogeneous Quantum Devices
pb: In the NISQ era, training and inference on heterogeneous quantum devices is hindered by limited qubits, device noise, and frequent online/offline transitions. Naive distributed QNN approaches destroy accuracy due to device heterogeneity and instability.
me: ArbiterQ applies personalized QNN models for each QPU via two uniform vector representations: model vector (logical-level parameters) and behavioral vector (hardware-level features). By sharing gradients among QPUs with similar behavioral vectors, the framework leverages parallelism while respecting heterogeneity. Additionally, shot-oriented inference scheduling provides fine-grained workload balancing and accuracy optimization.
nv: First framework using behavioral vector-based device personalization and gradient sharing for distributed NISQ QNN training with heterogeneous QPUs.
th: Personalized QNN models for heterogeneous quantum devices

t: Dual-Issue Execution of Mixed Integer and Floating-Point Workloads on Energy-Efficient In-Order RISC-V Cores
pb: Single-issue in-order cores have limited instruction-level parallelism (IPC); dual-issue cores offer potential performance boost but with increased area and energy overhead. Mixed integer and floating-point workloads are common but underserved.
me: Develops COPIFT methodology and RISC-V ISA extensions enabling low-cost dual-issue execution of mixed integer and floating-point instruction sequences. The approach couples integer and floating-point functional units to reduce area overhead while maintaining timing, leveraging instruction-type diversity to achieve parallelism.
nv: First methodology for lean dual-issue RISC-V cores with ISA extensions for efficient mixed integer-FP execution.
th: Lean dual-issue RISC-V for mixed integer-FP workloads

t: Towards Training Robustness Against Dynamic Errors in Quantum Machine Learning
pb: Quantum machine learning training assumes static error rates in QNNs, but quantum noise is dynamic across time and qubits, causing performance degradation even when aggregate error rates appear similar.
me: A novel noise-aware training strategy dynamically adjusts to standard and fatal error conditions during QNN optimization, incorporating low-complexity fatal-error detection to identify problematic error patterns and adapt training accordingly.
nv: Dynamic noise-aware training for quantum neural networks that adapts to time-varying and qubit-specific error conditions.

mx.accuracy: Competitive performance with leading NAT methods across varying error scenarios

th: Dynamic noise-aware training for quantum neural networks in NISQ era

t: Holistic Design towards Resource-Stringent Binary Vector Symbolic Architecture
pb: Binary Vector Symbolic Architecture offers minimal memory and fast execution but suffers from inferior inference accuracy and designs that prioritize algorithmic performance over hardware efficiency, limiting practical deployment on ultra-lightweight devices.
me: UniVSA co-optimizes binary VSA algorithms and hardware through novel lightweight modules and specialized design flow, achieving enhanced inference accuracy beyond state-of-the-art while reducing memory footprints and enabling efficient hardware execution on resource-constrained devices.
nv: Co-optimized algorithm-hardware framework for binary Vector Symbolic Architecture enabling both superior accuracy and hardware efficiency.

t: Invited paper: Enhancing Design Automation with Quantum Algorithms for Chip Design
pb: Cell placement optimization to minimize Half-Perimeter Wire Length is computationally expensive in classical approaches, limiting scalability for large designs; quantum and hybrid approaches may offer speedup.
me: A flexible quantum-hybrid placement optimization strategy minimizes HPWL through both custom Simulated Annealing and D-Wave Constrained Quadratic Model solvers, integrated with OpenROAD flow for layout and routing; validated on ASAP7 7nm PDK with real-world case studies.
nv: Quantum (D-Wave CQM) and hybrid optimization for chip cell placement integrated with industry-standard OpenROAD EDA flow.

t: EVA: An Efficient and Versatile Generative Engine for Targeted Discovery of Novel Analog Circuits
pb: Discovering entirely new, high-performance analog circuit topologies is an underexplored challenge; current AI methods focus on topology synthesis from known structures rather than generative discovery of novel designs.

t: EDGE: DBMS-Empowered Boolean Decomposition for GIG Synthesis
pb: Boolean decomposition-based logic synthesis is high-quality but computationally expensive, limiting application to large and complex logic functions in modern circuit design.
me: EDGE leverages modern database (DBMS) techniques to accelerate Boolean decomposition queries and candidate enumeration. Database queries replace iterative decomposition searches, exploiting relational query optimization to speedup candidate generation and evaluation for Gate-Inverter Graph synthesis.
nv: Application of DBMS query optimization to accelerate Boolean decomposition candidate exploration in logic synthesis.
th: Database acceleration for Boolean decomposition synthesis

t: SuperFast: Fast Supernet Training Using Initial Knowledge
pb: Once-for-all neural architecture search supernet training requires extremely high computational cost (72-83+ GPU days), limiting practical applicability despite enabling efficient multi-target deployment.
me: SuperFast employs two-stage training: (1) pretrains a small subnet within the supernet search space, (2) distributes this subnet's learned knowledge across the full supernet before main training. Knowledge propagation from small to large models enables faster convergence and better accuracy-cost tradeoffs. Plug-and-play workflow compatible with ElasticViT and NASViT.
nv: Knowledge distillation from small to large within once-for-all framework, reversing the conventional largest-model warmup approach.
th: Efficient supernet training via knowledge propagation

t: Graph-Guided Transfer Learning to Boost the Efficiency of System-Level Optimization of Analog/Mixed-Signal Circuits
pb: System-level optimization of analog/mixed-signal circuits requires expensive iterative circuit simulations; transfer learning has limited applicability across dissimilar architectures.
me: Combines reinforcement learning with graph attention networks (GAT) and a graph similarity detection method to identify electrical trade-offs; transfers learned policies across different circuit topologies by recognizing structural similarities.
nv: Graph similarity detection embedded in transfer learning to enable cross-architecture knowledge transfer for analog circuits.
th: Transfer learning for analog circuit synthesis

t: Late Breaking Results: Opera: An Open and Efficient Platform for Data-driven Synthesis of Analog Circuits
pb: Analog circuit synthesis is data-driven but bottlenecked by expensive circuit simulators in the synthesis loop; benchmarking methods requires exclusive access to commercial semiconductor technology.
me: Opera develops efficient surrogate models (neural networks) to replace expensive SPICE simulators; integrates surrogate models into OpenAI Gym-like environments for optimization; built on open-source 45nm semiconductor process for reproducibility.
nv: First open platform combining surrogate modeling and standardized RL environments for analog circuit synthesis.
th: Open surrogate-based platform for analog circuit synthesis

t: Synergistic Die-Level Router for Multi-FPGA System with Time-Division Multiplexing Optimization
pb: Multi-FPGA systems with multiple dies connected via TDM suffer from critical connection delays and routing congestion from super long lines (SLLs) between dies.
me: Die-level router that jointly optimizes routing topology and TDM timing ratios; reduces reliance on SLLs and critical path delays through topology-aware routing decisions.
nv: First die-level router co-optimizing routing topology and TDM ratios for multi-die FPGA systems.
th: Die-level routing and TDM optimization for multi-FPGA systems

t: Leopard: Hardware Pass-Through Remote Storage Access with Queue Concurrency for Edge Intelligent Workstations
pb: Edge workstations access remote cloud storage via complex software stacks and limited CPUs, causing 75% performance degradation by failing to saturate NVMe queue concurrency.
me: Leopard implements a custom NVMe controller on SmartNIC FPGA that emulates NVMe device and directly handles remote storage operations via parallelized hardware circuits; passes NVMe commands directly from edge OS to FPGA, bypassing CPU stacks.
nv: Hardware pass-through I/O controller for remote NVMe using SmartNIC FPGA, eliminating CPU-mediated software stacks.
th: FPGA-based pass-through remote storage controller

t: Hypnos: Memory Efficient Homomorphic Processing Unit
pb: FHE accelerators traditionally use Host+ACC topology assuming encrypted data already resides on-chip, neglecting PCIe bus inefficiency and memory access overhead; this leads to poor end-to-end performance dominated by data movement rather than computation.
me: Hypnos abstracts FHE operators into memory-efficient commands and combines them with a homomorphic encryption paged memory management system, significantly reducing memory access and execution time through intelligent data staging and on-chip cache hierarchy optimization.
nv: Paged memory management system tailored to FHE's irregular data access patterns, abstracting operations into memory-efficient commands that minimize off-chip communication.

mx.energy_efficiency: 27.6x vs CraterLake ASIC, 19.06x vs Poseidon FPGA for ResNet-20

th: Memory-efficient FHE accelerator via paged management and operator abstraction

t: Ares: High Performance Near-Storage Accelerator for FHE-based Private Set Intersection
pb: General-purpose FHE accelerators do not adequately address the unique requirements of Private Set Intersection applications, leading to suboptimal data handling, underutilization of hardware bandwidth, and inefficient deployment for PSI acceleration.
me: Ares is an FPGA accelerator co-designed with software, proposing Lazy Relinearization to optimize redundant PSI calculations, analyzing/decoupling PSI compute patterns into hardware kernels, and fully utilizing bandwidth and compute resources through specialized architecture design.
nv: Lazy Relinearization optimization eliminating redundant FHE operations in PSI without protocol changes, combined with hardware architecture specialized for PSI compute patterns.

mx.speedup: 47.99x vs CPU, 1.79x vs Poseidon, 1.93x vs FAB

th: PSI-specialized FHE accelerator with lazy relinearization optimization

t: Monolithic 3D FPGA Design and Synthesis with Back-End-of-Line Configuration Memories
pb: Conventional FPGAs use bulky Si SRAM for configuration, occupying area and increasing reconfigurable circuit overhead; this limits routing efficiency and increases latency for densely integrated FPGA designs.
me: Monolithic 3D FPGA uses amorphous oxide semiconductor (AOS) transistors in back-end-of-line (BEOL) layers: n-type (W-doped In₂O₃) and p-type (SnO) transistors replace bulky Si SRAM with lower-leakage configuration memory; AOS pass gates map FPGA switch/connection blocks above CLBs to increase proximity and reduce routing latency.
nv: BEOL-compatible AOS transistor-based configuration memory replacing Si SRAM in monolithic 3D FPGA, enabling denser routing matrices and reduced interconnect latency.
th: Monolithic 3D FPGA using BEOL AOS transistors for configuration memory

t: ACIM-QMM: Efficient Analog Computing-in-Memory Accelerator for QC-MDPC McEliece Cryptosystem
pb: Post-quantum cryptography (PQC) implementations like QC-MDPC McEliece suffer from high latency and large hardware overhead in digital computing paradigm.
me: ACIM-QMM leverages analog circuits and computing-in-memory to perform matrix operations required for QMM key generation and encryption, breaking the digital computing bottleneck while maintaining low relative error.
nv: First analog CIM accelerator for post-quantum cryptography, using analog computation paradigm to replace digital multiplication-accumulation in PQC algorithms.
th: analog CIM for post-quantum cryptography acceleration

t: DSPlacer: DSP Placement for FPGA-based CNN Accelerator
pb: FPGA-based CNN accelerator placement suffers from timing closure challenges; DSP placement directly impacts clock frequency and throughput but lacks automated optimization.
me: DSPlacer optimizes datapath DSP placement iteratively using graph convolutional network-based identification, DSP graph construction, min-cost-flow assignment, and integer linear programming (ILP) for cascade constraint legalization.
nv: First comprehensive framework combining GCN-based DSP identification, min-cost-flow assignment, and ILP-based cascade legalization for CNN accelerator timing optimization.

mx.other: 32% WNS improvement vs Vivado, 65% vs AMF-Placer

th: automated DSP placement for FPGA CNN accelerators

t: GSAcc: Accelerate 3D Gaussian Splatting via Depth Speculation and Gaussian-centric Rasterization
pb: GPU-based 3D Gaussian Splatting rendering suffers from insufficient parallelism in sequential pipeline stages and large memory overhead for intermediate results.
me: GSAcc introduces Gaussian depth speculation to parallelize preprocessing and sorting. A Gaussian-centric dataflow interleaves preprocessing and rasterization, executing all steps concurrently without storing intermediates. Dedicated hardware accelerates sorting and rasterization.
nv: Gaussian-centric dataflow interleaving preprocessing and rasterization to eliminate intermediate storage and enable full parallelism.
th: Hardware accelerator for efficient 3D Gaussian Splatting rendering

t: NSFlow: An End-to-End FPGA Framework with Scalable Dataflow Architecture for Neuro-Symbolic AI
pb: Neuro-Symbolic AI workloads exhibit heterogeneous kernels and unique memory access patterns unsuitable for general-purpose ML accelerators (CPU/GPU/TPU).
me: NSFlow features a design architecture generator identifying data dependencies and creating optimized dataflows, plus a reconfigurable FPGA array with flexible compute units, reorganizable memory, and mixed-precision capabilities.
nv: Architecture generator synthesizing optimized FPGA dataflows from NSAI workload data dependencies, enabling end-to-end acceleration.

mx.speedup: 31x vs Jetson TX2, >2x vs GPU, 8x vs TPU, >3x vs Xilinx DPU

th: FPGA dataflow framework for neuro-symbolic AI acceleration

t: CHORD: Composable Hybrid Optical Reconfigurable Diffractive Framework For Optical Neural Network
pb: Diffractive optical neural networks (DONNs) offer ultra-parallel, high-efficiency computing via freespace light propagation, but lack reconfigurability due to fixed post-fabrication optical structures, limiting practical deployment for dynamic AI workloads.
me: CHORD combines composable hybrid optical/photonic design with full-system learnability. Fixed fabricated optical hardware is repurposed through differentiable learning of system variables, achieving reconfigurability. Hybrid design leverages integrated photonic reconfigurability with free-space diffractive ultra-parallelism.
nv: First composable hybrid optical/photonic DONN architecture enabling exponentially expanded functional space through full-system differentiable learning while maintaining fixed post-fabrication hardware.
th: Hybrid optical/photonic reconfigurable DONN with learnable system variables

t: SimPhony: A Device-Circuit-Architecture Cross-Layer Modeling and Simulation Framework for Heterogeneous Electronic-Photonic AI System
pb: Electronic-photonic integrated circuits (EPICs) for AI require innovations across devices, circuits, architecture, and design automation. Lack of unified simulation framework prevents exploration of hardware innovations and evaluation on common benchmarks.
me: SimPhony provides cross-layer modeling and simulation: generic extensible hardware topology for heterogeneous multi-core photonic tensor cores; optics-specific dataflow with multi-dimensional parallelism; data-aware energy modeling with device responses, area estimation, link budget and bandwidth-adaptive memory; seamless hardware/software co-simulation integration with model training frameworks.
nv: First unified cross-layer simulation framework for electronic-photonic AI systems supporting optics-specific dataflow modeling beyond spatial/temporal dimensions.

mx.other: cross-layer fidelity and simulation speed metrics not specified

th: Cross-layer simulation framework for heterogeneous electronic-photonic AI systems

t: Late Breaking Results: FPGen-3D: Automated Framework for 3D-FPGA Architecture Generation and Exploration
pb: FPGA design space exploration is limited by 2D constraints; exploring 3D FPGA architectures with vertical connections requires manual and tedious design efforts, preventing efficient navigation of 3D design space.
me: FPGen-3D automates 3D FPGA architecture generation from user-defined parameters, producing synthesizable RTL, routing results, and programming bitstreams. Explores vertical connection strategies via 3D switch blocks (SB) and 3D configurable logic blocks (CLB).
nv: Automated framework for 3D FPGA architecture generation enabling systematic exploration of vertical connection strategies (3D SB and CLB designs).
th: Automated 3D FPGA architecture generation and exploration framework

t: Towards In-Situ Neuromorphic Computing Architecture for Event Stream Super-Resolution
pb: Event-based cameras generate sparse, low-resolution event streams mitigating motion blur in high-speed scenarios but lacking sufficient spatial resolution. Super-resolution of event streams requires efficient neuromorphic hardware architecture avoiding excessive intermediate storage.
me: Proposes spiking neural network (SNN) based accelerator with hardware-friendly designs: simplified neuron models, optimized convolutions, hierarchical parallel array. Novel Kernel-Channel-Timestamp-Row (KCTR) dataflow with dual-pipeline structure achieves in-situ computing, eliminating inter-layer spike storage.
nv: KCTR dataflow with dual-pipeline enabling in-situ computing without intermediate layer storage, specifically designed for neuromorphic event stream processing.
th: In-situ neuromorphic accelerator for event stream super-resolution with KCTR dataflow

t: ABC-FHE: A Resource-Efficient Accelerator Enabling Bootstrappable Parameters for Client-Side Fully Homomorphic Encryption
pb: Client-side Fully Homomorphic Encryption (FHE) computations remain a bottleneck, particularly under bootstrappable parameter configurations involving encoding, encryption, decoding, and decryption for large parameters, requiring 10,000-fold more computation than plaintext processing.
me: ABC-FHE employs a streaming architecture with a reconfigurable Fourier engine capable of switching between NTT (Number-Theoretic Transform) and FFT (Fast Fourier Transform) modes. It includes an on-chip pseudo-random number generator and unified on-the-fly twiddle factor generator to reduce memory demands, with optimized task scheduling to enhance CKKS client-side processing, reducing off-chip memory access.
nv: Reconfigurable dual-mode Fourier engine (NTT/FFT) with on-chip PRNG and unified twiddle generation to eliminate bottlenecks in bootstrappable FHE parameter processing while minimizing area.

mx.speedup: 1112x encoding/encryption vs CPU, 214x vs SOTA accelerator; 963x decoding/decryption vs CPU, 82x vs SOTA

th: Reconfigurable ASIC for client-side FHE with dual Fourier engine

t: CAE-DFKD: Bridging the Transferability Gap in Data-Free Knowledge Distillation
pb: Existing data-free knowledge distillation (DFKD) methods focus on image-level recognition performance without addressing transferability of learned representations to downstream tasks.
me: Proposes Category-Aware Embedding DFKD (CAE-DFKD) that operates at the embedding level rather than image level; alters generator training paradigm to improve representation quality and downstream task transfer.
nv: Embedding-level knowledge distillation approach that prioritizes representation transferability over image-level metrics.

mx.other: transferability on downstream tasks

th: Embedding-level knowledge distillation for improved transferability

t: zkVC: Fast Zero-Knowledge Proof for Private and Verifiable Computing
pb: Zero-knowledge proofs (ZKP), especially zkSNARKs, remain computationally intensive for basic operations like matrix multiplication, requiring extensive constraint systems and creating significant overhead.
me: Proposes zkVC with optimized ZKP modules including Constraint-reduced Polynomial Circuit (CRPC) for reducing constraint overhead and Prefix-Sum Query (PSQ) for efficient aggregation; specializes in accelerating matrix multiplication proofs.
nv: Constraint-reduced polynomial circuits that minimize ZKP constraint overhead while maintaining proof security.

mx.speedup: 12x faster proof generation vs prior methods

th: Constraint-reduced zero-knowledge proofs for fast matrix verification

t: Routability-aware Packing for High-density Nonvolatile FPGAs
pb: NVFPGAs with MLC NVMs achieve high logic density but suffer from severely degraded CLB intra-routability, causing long packing times in CAD flow.
me: Routability-aware re-pair stage adjusts LUT assignments to reduce congestion and improve intra-routability; exploits structural equivalence of MLC LUTs to eliminate redundant routing attempts during packing.
nv: LUT assignment re-pairing specifically targeting MLC routing topology to reduce congestion without full re-placement.
th: NVFPGA packing optimization

t: DyREM: Dynamically Mitigating Quantum Readout Error with Embedded Accelerator
pb: Quantum readout error mitigation requires on-the-fly computation of large mitigation matrices, incurring high latency and memory overhead that limits practical quantum computing scale.
me: DyREM leverages sparsity in quantum state probability distributions to dynamically downsample mitigation matrices. An embedded accelerator computes tensor products using gating to skip nonzero quantum state computations.
nv: Sparsity-aware dynamic matrix downsampling and gated computation for quantum readout error mitigation.

mx.other: 1.03x-1.15x fidelity

th: Quantum readout acceleration

t: SDISC: A Spike-Driven Human-Machine Interface with In-Situ Computing for Real-Time Low-Power Interaction
pb: Bio-signal processing for HMI (EMG, EEG) incurs high latency and power using conventional hardware; frame-based methods cannot achieve real-time energy-efficient edge inference.
me: SDISC combines: (1) spike-driven feature extraction (>10x sparsity vs frame-based), (2) RRAM-based in-situ SNN computation (4.09 TOPS/W), (3) Spike-Activity-Distillation and Aid-Loser-Only recovery schemes to handle RRAM non-ideality and long-term drift.
nv: Spike-driven bioprocessing with RRAM in-situ computing and device-aware algorithm design for long-horizon HMI.

mx.other: 34 µs latency

th: Neuromorphic HMI accelerator

t: SAPO: Improving the Scalability and Accuracy of Quantum Linear Solver for Portfolio Optimization
pb: Quantum linear solvers for portfolio optimization suffer from poor scalability or insufficient accuracy; existing quantum HHL-based methods cannot efficiently handle large-scale financial problems with acceptable precision.
me: SAPO extends the HHL algorithm by integrating mean-variance financial theory into the quantum circuit design via equivalent transformations to improve scalability, and applies a min-max eigenvalue model calibrated on historical market data to refine quantum circuit parameters for high accuracy.
nv: First to jointly optimize quantum circuit design and parameter settings using financial domain knowledge and historical data characteristics.
th: Quantum-accelerated financial optimization

t: BOSON-1: Understanding and Enabling Physically-Robust Photonic Inverse Design with Adaptive Variation-Aware Subspace Optimization
pb: Nanophotonic inverse design structures discovered via adjoint methods are numerically plausible but difficult to fabricate and highly sensitive to physical variations. Discrete material distributions create numerous local optima, causing gradient-based methods to converge suboptimally.
me: BOSON-1 formulates inverse design as a fabrication-restricted, discrete, probabilistic optimization problem. It explicitly considers fabrication constraints, uses dense target-enhanced gradient flows to mitigate misleading local optima, and applies conditional subspace optimization with adaptive sampling-based robust optimization.
nv: End-to-end variation-aware inverse design framework that differentiably optimizes within the fabricable subspace, combining robust optimization with adaptive sampling to escape local optima.
th: Fabrication-aware photonic inverse design with variation robustness

t: Exploring Dendritic Computation in Bio-Inspired Architectures for Dynamic Programming
pb: Finding shortest paths in graphs using bio-inspired neuromorphic architectures rather than conventional sequential algorithms. Neuromorphic systems offer alternative computational paradigm with different efficiency/latency tradeoffs.
me: Model each graph node as leaky integrate-and-fire (LIF) neuron with dendritic delay line for synaptic propagation and somatic feedback controlling delay. Formulate shortest path as finding earliest neuron firing times, decomposing into sub-problems iteratively solved via backward tracing. Countdown counters implement forward propagation; eligibility traces incorporate edge costs.
nv: Formulating dynamic programming shortest path in spiking neural networks using spike timing as solution mechanism.

mx.other: scalability demonstrated on real graphs

th: neuromorphic graph algorithms

t: Multi-Sensor Data Fusion for Enhanced Detection of Laser Fault Injection Attacks in Cryptographic Hardware: Practical Results
pb: Detecting laser fault injection attacks on cryptographic hardware deployed in FPGAs. Laser attacks offer high precision and temporal control, making them difficult to detect with single sensors.
me: Low-cost detection scheme using Time-to-Digital Converters (TDCs) to sense IR voltage drops induced by laser illumination. Multi-sensor fusion approach with minimum two sensors improves detection reliability and reduces false alarms.
nv: Multi-sensor TDC-based fusion achieving high detection rate with minimal false alarms against laser fault injection.

mx.other: detection rate, false alarm rate

th: laser-attack detection

t: KalmMind: A Configurable Kalman Filter Design Framework for Embedded Brain-Computer Interfaces
pb: Deploying Kalman Filter motion prediction from brain signals in resource-constrained embedded brain-computer interface systems. Limited optimization of KF for embedded BCI deployment.
me: Framework for designing Kalman Filter hardware accelerators specialized for BCI applications. Provides tunable design-space exploration enabling balance between latency and accuracy.
nv: Configurable KF accelerator framework enabling latency-accuracy optimization for embedded BCI deployment.

mx.other: latency improvement, accuracy improvement

th: specialized BCI accelerators

t: CAS-PUF: Current-Mode Array-Type Strong PUF for Secure Computing in Area Constrained SoCs
pb: Strong PUFs are essential for secure SoCs but traditional designs consume excessive area, preventing deployment in area-constrained IoT and mobile applications requiring hardware-based cryptographic key generation and device authentication.
me: Proposes Current-mode Array-type Strong PUF (CAS-PUF) based on a current source topology using only six minimum-size transistors; architecture is tolerant to power supply variation and enables efficient Challenge-Response Pair generation.
nv: Minimal-transistor current-mode strong PUF achieving high CRP capacity with negligible area overhead.
th: Area-efficient strong PUF for IoT

t: Neural Circuit Parameter Prediction for Efficient Quantum Data Loading
pb: Quantum data loading—encoding classical data into quantum states—is a critical bottleneck in quantum machine learning; existing methods achieve high per-sample accuracy but lack efficiency for large-scale batch loading.
me: Proposes Neural Circuit Parameter Prediction using classical deep neural networks to predict parameterized quantum circuit parameters directly from input data; leverages batch inference capability of DNNs; introduces real-valued circuit parameterization and three-phase training strategy for improved efficiency.
nv: DNN-based parameter prediction for quantum circuits enabling efficient batch quantum data loading.
th: Neural network-predicted quantum circuits

t: PEARL: FPGA-Based Reinforcement Learning Acceleration with Pipelined Parallel Environments
pb: CPU-based RL frameworks struggle with slow multi-environment update computation; parallelizing environments requires efficient data transfer and computation overlap.
me: FPGA-based framework that instantiates multiple parallel environments with pipelined execution scheme. Pipeline design hides data transfer latency within computation time. Flexible environment definition allows users to add custom environments. Supports scaling from 1024 to 43008+ environments.
nv: Pipelined parallel environment architecture that overlaps data transfer with computation, eliminating I/O bottleneck for multi-environment RL training.

mx.other: 3% power increase at 43008 envs, 2.24x LUT, 3.08x FF utilization

th: FPGA-accelerated parallel RL environments via pipelined dataflow

t: CPP-SGS: Cycle-Accurate Power Prediction Framework via SNN and Genetic Signal Selection
pb: Accurate cycle-by-cycle power prediction requires monitoring numerous signals; traditional approaches face scalability and computational overhead issues in runtime power management.
me: Combines Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) for temporal power dynamics modeling with Genetic Algorithms (GAs) for signal feature selection. GAs identify the most relevant subset of signals to feed into SNNs, reducing model size and inference latency for real-time deployment.
nv: Integration of SNNs (inherently efficient for temporal data) with GA-based feature selection to minimize model complexity while maintaining prediction accuracy.

mx.other: NRMSE < 1.6%

th: SNN-based cycle-accurate power prediction with GA feature selection

t: Nanoelectromechanical Binary Comparator for Edge-Computing Applications
pb: Binary comparison is fundamental in arithmetic and ML algorithms but CMOS implementations waste power on standby; harsh edge environments (high temperature, radiation) require robust comparators.
me: Implements binary comparators using 4-terminal nanoelectromechanical (NEM) relays: single 1-bit magnitude and equality comparators use only 6 devices vs 9 transistors in CMOS. Fabricated on silicon-on-insulator substrate. Scalable tree-based topology for higher-order comparators achieves ~47% device reduction vs CMOS for 64-bit comparators.
nv: First silicon-fabricated NEM relay comparators demonstrating higher integration density, extreme temperature tolerance (300°C), radiation hardness (>1 Mrad), and zero standby power.
th: NEM relay comparators for radiation-hard edge computing

t: Low-Latency Digital Feedback for Stochastic Quantum Calibration Using Cryogenic CMOS
pb: Quantum gate calibration requires low-latency feedback between quantum systems and classical control hardware to track drifting parameters; implementing this feedback without on-board compute (FPGA/ASIC) is impossible.
me: Analyzes stochastic gate calibration protocol performance under various latency conditions; synthesizes classical control logic in 28nm CMOS with simulations extended to 14nm FinFET and cryogenic temperatures to demonstrate feasibility and performance characteristics.
nv: Demonstrates that quantum calibration protocols can be easily implemented within contemporary control architectures for low-latency performance without significant power or resource overhead.
th: Cryogenic ASIC control for quantum gate calibration

t: Multi-Partner Project: Key Enabling Technologies for Cognitive Computing Continuum - MYRTUS Project Perspective
pb: Building distributed, heterogeneous computing systems across edge-fog-cloud continuum requires abstractions, orchestration mechanisms, and design environments that are currently lacking.
me: Delivers abstractions for heterogeneous resource management, cognitive orchestration mechanisms for resource allocation, and unified design environment for building and operating distributed systems across edge-fog-cloud continuum.
nv: Integrated design environment and cognitive orchestration for unified edge-fog-cloud computing continuum.
th: Cognitive orchestration for edge-fog-cloud continuum

t: Late Breaking Results: Improving Deep SNNs with Gradient Clipping and Noise Exploitation in Neuromorphic Devices
pb: Deep SNNs trained with soft resets are computationally expensive and unsuitable for neuromorphic hardware; hard reset-based SNNs suffer performance degradation without gradient clipping.
me: Proposes gradient clipping technique for hard reset-based SNN training; explores exploitation of device noise to enhance learning performance; evaluates across multiple datasets and models.
nv: Device noise can be leveraged to enhance SNN learning performance in hard reset regime, contrary to treating noise as pure interference.
th: Noise-aware SNN training for neuromorphic hardware

t: Solving the Cold-Start Problem for the Edge: Clustering and Adaptive Deep Learning for Emotion Detection
pb: Personalized edge ML systems face cold-start problem when new users lack labeled data, and deployment constraints limit model complexity for resource-constrained edge devices.
me: CLEAR (Clustering and Learning for Emotion Adaptive Recognition) combines unsupervised clustering for user grouping with fine-tuning on minimal labeled data, deployed on Coral Edge TPU and Movidius Neural Compute Stick 2.
nv: Data-driven clustering enables cold-start personalization without labeled data for new users, bridging population-wide and fully personalized models.

mx.accuracy: 81.9% with clustering (vs 75% baseline), 86.34% fear detection with fine-tuning

th: clustering-based personalization for edge emotion detection

t: Online Learning for Dynamic Structural Characterization in Electron Energy Loss Spectroscopy
pb: High-speed in-situ EELS data acquisition (400 fps) with low SNR requires real-time processing for dynamic structural tracking without offline training bottleneck.
me: Spiking neural network (SNN)-based Variational Autoencoder (VAE) embeds spectral data for structural prediction with online learning implemented on FPGA, achieving 28.3 dB SNR and 25.2×–93.7× latency reduction.
nv: First fully online learning hardware solution combining SNNs with VAEs for real-time EELS structural tracking without offline training.
th: online SNN-VAE on FPGA for materials characterization

t: ASNPC: An Automated Generation Framework for SNN and Neuromorphic Processor Co-Design
pb: SNN and neuromorphic processor design typically prioritize single optimization criterion; hardware-algorithm codesign space is vast with expensive function evaluations.
me: ASNPC employs surrogate-based multi-objective optimization (MOTPE) to explore mixed-variable codesign space, automatically generates RTL from hardware templates, feeding hardware metrics back for iterative Pareto solution discovery.
nv: Surrogate-based multi-objective optimization with automatic RTL generation enables efficient hardware-algorithm codesign for SNNs.
th: hardware-algorithm codesign for SNNs via multi-objective optimization

t: PICBench: Benchmarking LLMs for Photonic Integrated Circuits Design
pb: LLMs show promise for digital chip design automation but photonic integrated circuit design remains unexplored; PIC design is time-consuming and repetitive.
me: PICBench provides benchmark framework for evaluating LLM-based PIC netlist generation, assesses syntax and functionality via automatic simulation comparison against expert solutions, tests various LLMs and prompt engineering strategies.
nv: First LLM benchmarking and evaluation framework specifically for photonic integrated circuit design automation.

mx.accuracy: LLM correctness evaluated via simulation comparison

th: LLM benchmarking for photonic circuit design

t: Late Breaking Results: Approximated LUT-Based Neural Networks for FPGA Accelerated Inference
pb: FPGA neural network acceleration via LUT-based matrix multiplication suffers from limited arithmetic intensity and memory bandwidth bottlenecks, constraining throughput and efficiency.
me: LUT-MU is an approximated LUT-based matrix multiplication architecture with optimized memory distribution and pipeline design to maximize on-chip memory bandwidth utilization and arithmetic intensity.
nv: Memory-optimized pipeline design for LUT-based matrix multiplication addressing FPGA bandwidth and arithmetic intensity constraints.
th: Memory-optimized LUT-based neural network acceleration for FPGA edge inference

t: SoftCUDA: Running CUDA on Softcore GPU
pb: Softcore GPU designs on FPGAs lack comprehensive software stack support, making it challenging to translate CUDA code to alternative programming models while maintaining feature parity, limiting adoption across diverse parallel workloads.
me: SoftCUDA provides a comprehensive framework that compiles and executes unmodified CUDA applications on the Vortex softcore GPU implemented on FPGAs. The framework leverages FPGA reconfigurability while maintaining a user-friendly CUDA interface for transparent integration with existing CUDA ecosystems.
nv: End-to-end CUDA support on softcore GPU architectures, enabling unmodified CUDA applications to run directly on FPGA platforms without translation to alternative programming models.
th: CUDA support for FPGA-based softcore GPUs

t: Performance Modeling and Comparisons of an FPGA-based Direct Simulation Monte Carlo Solver
pb: DSMC simulations encounter race conditions when parallelizing collision evaluation in conventional implementations, limiting speedup on multi-core and many-core platforms.
me: The solver employs a spatially-parallel collision evaluation algorithm implemented on FPGA, which organizes collision processing by spatial domain to eliminate synchronization race conditions inherent in conventional parallel DSMC. The FPGA leverages custom hardware parallelism and memory hierarchies tailored for different particle count regimes, particularly low-particle scenarios typical in microscale flows.
nv: Spatially-parallel collision evaluation algorithm that eliminates race conditions in DSMC parallelization.

mx.speedup: 5.5× vs CPU, 1.5× vs GPU (low particle counts)

th: Parallel DSMC collision evaluation on FPGA

t: DRSA: Accelerating Macro Placement on Commercial FPGAs
pb: FPGA macro-component placement in DynaRapid creates a bottleneck where the existing greedy placement strategy causes significant frequency degradation, limiting the practical benefits of macro-based fast compilation.
me: DRSA replaces greedy placement with simulated annealing optimization specifically tailored for macro-level components in DynaRapid. The simulated annealing algorithm iteratively refines macro positions to minimize frequency loss while maintaining fast placement execution, navigating the placement design space more effectively than greedy approaches.
nv: Simulated annealing-based macro placer designed for DynaRapid that eliminates frequency degradation while preserving the fast compilation benefits of macro-hierarchical design.

mx.other: frequency degradation elimination, placement time reduction

th: macro-based FPGA placement optimization

t: Accelerating Scientific Model Optimization with a Pipelined FPGA-Based Differential Evolution Engine
pb: Differential Evolution optimization for complex scientific models with stiff differential equations requires intensive computation. Current CPU and GPU implementations suffer from high latency and energy consumption when solving models like Hodgkin-Huxley and circadian rhythms.
me: The architecture employs a pipelined FPGA design that leverages deep pipelines and parallel memory access patterns. Double-precision floating-point arithmetic and adaptive numerical integration techniques handle stiff differential equations. The modular design enables seamless customization for different scientific models and integration methods.
nv: A modular, pipelined FPGA architecture specifically optimized for Differential Evolution applied to scientific model optimization.
th: FPGA-accelerated differential evolution

t: BCIM: A Bit-Serial Approach for Block-Cipher-in-Memory
pb: Existing in-memory block cipher implementations suffer from timing-based side-channel vulnerabilities and energy inefficiency in bit-parallel designs. The challenge is providing both constant-time execution and high-throughput block cipher operations within memory subsystems.
me: BCIM employs a bit-serial approach combined with column-wise SIMD processing to achieve constant-time block cipher execution. The constant-time nature of bit-serial execution inherently resists timing-based side-channel attacks. Architectural and circuit-level innovations minimize memory footprint for key storage and improve peak operating frequency and energy efficiency.
nv: Exploiting bit-serial execution with column-wise SIMD processing to achieve both constant-time side-channel resilience and high-throughput block cipher operations in-memory.

mx.speedup: substantial vs bit-parallel IMC, competitive vs bitsliced software
mx.energy: orders of magnitude improvement over bitsliced software on CPU/MCU

th: constant-time in-memory cryptography via bit-serial SIMD

t: APR-OIS: A Near-Sensor Point Cloud Pre-Processing Accelerator on FPGA
pb: Raw point clouds from 3D sensors (LiDAR, RGB-D cameras) contain enormous numbers of points and require expensive down-sampling to reduce data while preserving spatial structure before use in point cloud applications.
me: The paper proposes APR-OIS (Approximate Octree-Indexed Sampling), an approximation method that accelerates Octree-based down-sampling by exploiting spatial proximity properties of Octree nodes. The method is implemented as an FPGA-based accelerator functioning as a near-sensor processor on raw 3D sensor data.
nv: An approximation method (APR-OIS) that achieves significant acceleration in Octree-based point cloud down-sampling with minimal accuracy loss.

t: QuCLEAR: Clifford Extraction and Absorption for Quantum Circuit Optimization

Second, Clifford Absorption leverages the classical simulatability of Clifford circuits to compute their effect analytically and absorb (classically post-process) the extracted Clifford subcircuit rather than executing it on quantum hardware, eliminating those gates entirely from the quantum circuit.

t: LegoZK: A Dynamically Reconfigurable Accelerator for Zero-Knowledge Proof

GBU integrates with conventional edge GPUs to support a wide range of AR/VR applications.

t: LaZagna: An Open-Source Framework for Flexible 3D FPGA Architectural Exploration
