To narrow the remaining gap, the authors propose a small x86 ISA extension called MQX (multi-word extension) that adds three new instructions targeting multi-precision modular arithmetic patterns common in NTT and BLAS. MQX cuts the slowdown relative to ASICs to as low as 35x per core; a roofline analysis of multi-core scaling shows that top-tier server CPUs with MQX can approach ASIC-level throughput.
nv: The MQX (multi-word extension) ISA extension — just three new AVX-512 instructions targeting multi-precision modular arithmetic — that closes much of the remaining gap between x86 CPUs and cryptographic ASICs for NTT and large-integer BLAS.

t: FedProphet: Memory-Efficient Federated Adversarial Training via Robust and Consistent Cascade Learning
pb: Federated Adversarial Training (FAT) requires large models to attain high accuracy and robustness, but memory-constrained edge devices cannot fit full-model training; existing memory-efficient FL methods sacrifice accuracy or robustness through objective inconsistency between local and global models.
me: FedProphet uses adversarial cascade learning: the full model is split into small sequential modules, each trained on one class of devices. Strong convexity regularization on each module's loss ensures local module objectives remain consistent with the global adversarial loss. A server-side coordinator performs Adaptive Perturbation Adjustment (APA) to balance utility vs. robustness trade-off dynamically, and Differentiated Module Assignment (DMA) to assign modules to heterogeneous devices, mitigating objective inconsistency across rounds.

t: VoLUT: Efficient Volumetric streaming enhanced by LUT-based super-resolution
pb: 3D volumetric video streaming requires extremely high bandwidth; downsampling before transmission and upsampling via super-resolution at the receiver is needed, but existing 3D SR algorithms are too slow for real-time use on commodity mobile devices.
me: VoLUT has a two-stage SR pipeline. Stage 1 (dilated kNN interpolation): broader spatial context via dilated k-nearest neighbor search for initial upsampling; octree parallelism accelerates the kNN computation; neighbor relationships are reused across upsampling steps. Stage 2 (LUT refinement): coordinates of upsampled points are normalized to [0,1], quantized into b discrete bins per axis (bin=128 by default), and looked up in a precomputed 3D LUT that stores high-resolution position offsets (RF=4 receptive field, bin=128 yields 1.6GB LUT). The LUT is built offline from a trained NN model. MPC (Model Predictive Control)-based adaptive bitrate algorithm dynamically selects downsampling rate based on network conditions, streaming a continuous range of quality levels.
nv: First system to run high-quality 3D point cloud super-resolution on commodity mobile devices at line-rate, using offline NN-to-LUT conversion with position encoding quantization and dilated kNN interpolation, combined with MPC-based continuous ABR streaming.

th: Neuromorphic biomedical signal processing

t: Layer-Specific Hardware Pooling Designs for CNN Accelerators
pb: CNN accelerator design typically uses uniform pooling (e.g., max pooling only), but different layers may benefit from different pooling strategies.
me: Design-space exploration of combinatorial pooling techniques: combinations of Max pooling with deviation-based methods (AAD, BWAD, AMD) across different CNN layers. Evaluated on AlexNet, UNet, VGG-16. FPGA synthesis on Xilinx Zedboard; ASIC synthesis in Cadence 45nm.
nv: Layer-specific pooling optimization; first systematic exploration of combinatorial pooling in CNN accelerators; demonstrates that mixed pooling strategies outperform uniform approaches.
th: Layer-specific optimization for CNN accelerators

t: 8GHz Multi-Phase Ring VCO Design with Wide Tuning Range for SerDes Applications in 6nm FinFET Process
pb: SerDes applications require voltage-controlled oscillators with wide frequency tuning range, low phase noise, and operation across PVT variations.
me: 8-phase pseudo Differential Ring Oscillator design in 6nm FinFET (0.8V ±5%, -40 to +125°C). Two Basic Delay Cell architectures (BDC-1, BDC-2) proposed and compared.
nv: Multi-phase ring VCO design optimized for 6nm FinFET; comparison of delay cell architectures for wide tuning range.
th: Optimized analog circuit design for high-speed I/O

t: Design of Manchester Carry Chain Hybrid Adder for MASH 1-1-1 Delta Sigma Modulator for Fractional-N Frequency Synthesizers
pb: MASH 1-1-1 Delta Sigma Modulators for fractional-N frequency synthesizers require high-speed, low-power adders with minimal worst-case delay.
me: Novel high-speed hybrid adder combining Carry-Look-Ahead and Carry-Select using Domino Logic and Manchester Carry Chain topology. Includes negative-edge triggered low-power partially static flip-flop for sampling.
nv: Hybrid CLA-Carry-Select topology optimized for DSM; Manchester Carry Chain in Domino Logic; application-specific flip-flop design.
th: Optimized arithmetic for analog/mixed-signal systems

t: NSGA-RM: NSGA-II Evolved Performance Optimized Non-Homogeneous Recursive Polynomial Multiplier Architectures
pb: Polynomial multiplication in finite fields is critical for cryptographic systems but hardware efficiency optimization requires exploring large design spaces. Existing heuristic approaches (Hybrid Recursive Multiplier) may miss optimal solutions.
me: NSGA-II (Non-dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm II) applied to recursive multiplier design space. Explores configurations of state-of-the-art multipliers (MNHKA, MNHOKA variants). Solutions synthesized with Cadence Genus for GPDK 45nm technology.
nv: NSGA-II genetic algorithm optimization for polynomial multiplier architecture design, systematically exploring non-homogeneous recursive multiplier configurations to achieve Pareto-optimal solutions.
th: GA-driven optimization for cryptographic arithmetic

t: Advancing Rehabilitation Through Low Weight Hand Assistive System: Design and Impact Analysis
pb: Individuals with impaired hand function due to stroke, spinal cord injuries, and neuromuscular disorders struggle with daily activities and rehabilitation. Existing assistive devices are often slow and lack real-time feedback.
me: Smart Hand Mobility Assistive Device integrating: (1) Advanced sensor technology for finger movement detection, (2) Real-time data processing for immediate feedback, (3) Adaptive actuation for motor amplification. Mobile application provides physiotherapy exercises and interactive therapeutic games. Multiple control modes: manual assistance, cyclic training, task-specific routines.
nv: Lightweight smart hand assistive device with integrated real-time feedback, adaptive actuation, and multi-modal mobile app for progressive hand function rehabilitation.

mx.target_users: stroke, spinal cord injury, neuromuscular disorder patients
mx.evaluation: grip strength, dexterity, overall hand function

th: Smart assistive devices for rehabilitation

t: Startup Circuit for Relaxation Oscillators with Low Functional Current and Minimal Area
pb: Low-power relaxation oscillators suffer from long startup times, which is critical in ultra-low-power applications like timekeeping and sensor interfaces. Existing startup circuits either increase functional current or require significant area overhead.
me: A two-stage startup technique that initializes the ring oscillator in open-loop mode (with injected current to charge internal nodes) and then switches to closed-loop once frequency settles. Uses current mirrors and digital circuits for lightweight implementation.
nv: Open-to-closed-loop transition startup methodology that achieves 3x faster startup (466µs → 150µs) without increasing functional current; minimal area overhead using current mirrors and digital logic.
th: Ultra-Low-Power Analog Design

t: Optimization of Sub-Threshold Standard Cells for Energy Efficient Designs
pb: Ultra-low-power IC designs require aggressive voltage scaling, but standard foundry libraries optimized for nominal voltage (1.2V) introduce significant performance penalties at subthreshold (< 500mV) voltages, necessitating custom cell libraries.
me: Comprehensive methodology for subthreshold standard cell library design using SPEA-2 multi-objective genetic algorithm for optimal transistor sizing. Library validated on RISC-V processors and EPFL benchmark circuits against nominal (1.2V) and near-threshold (600mV) foundry baselines.
nv: Genetic algorithm-driven multi-objective optimization for subthreshold standard cells achieving 44% average energy efficiency improvement; systematic validation on both processors and benchmark circuits.
th: Ultra-Low-Power Design & Optimization

t: CMOSP18 FD-SOI Technology Based MCU Achieving High Performance of 1.2GHz Using High Speed, Optimized Leakage & High Density Tightly Coupled Memory (TCM)
pb: Microcontroller units (MCUs) require both high performance (>1GHz) and low-leakage operation. Tightly coupled memories (TCM) are critical for processor performance but consume significant power and area. Optimizing TCM for both speed and leakage is challenging without degrading performance.
me: Two TCM variants in CMOSP18 FD-SOI technology: (1) performance-optimized instances for TCM placed closer to core (standard timing); (2) leakage-optimized instances for far TCM placement (reduced VDD, optimized gates). Both use high-density bitcells to reduce area and RC delay.
nv: Dual-variant TCM optimization strategy targeting spatial proximity within same core: performance optimization for near-core TCM, leakage optimization for distant TCM, using high-density bitcell design.
th: Embedded Memory & Microcontroller Design

t: Multi-Object Detection Through Meta-Training in Resource-Constrained UAV-Based Surveillance Applications
pb: Object detection in UAV surveillance requires real-time performance on resource-constrained edge devices. Domain variation (nighttime, crowds, weather, small objects) degrades detection accuracy, and standard models trained on limited domains generalize poorly to real-world conditions.
me: Meta-training framework for domain generalization (adaptation): YOLO models trained iteratively across diverse domains (nighttime, crowds, sunny weather, small objects) using gradient descent-based optimization. Transfer learning enables model to learn domain-adaptive features. Multiple YOLO configurations and public/custom datasets tested.
nv: Meta-training approach for domain generalization in YOLO-based object detection; demonstrates improved generalization across environmental adversities in UAV surveillance without single-domain overfitting.
